Applicant and Manufacturer: Dresser Wayne Fuel Equipment (Shanghai) Co., Ltd, 51 Daxiu Road, Pudong, 201201 Shanghai, China

Certified type: fuel dispenser, Type: Global Century

Recommendation: R 117-1 (2007) "Dynamic measuring systems for liquids other than water"
Accuracy class: 0,5 → 0.5

Test reports: No. NMi-16200580-03 dated 18 November 2016, 28 pages. Role: type_evaluation_report (it says "the results of tests and examinations provided in the associated report(s)" — it's the OIML Type Evaluation Report mentioned). I'll call it type_evaluation_report.

Documentation folders: T10463-1 (construction documentation), TC7211-1, TC7212-6 (Pulsers), TC7213-2, TC7210-1. These could be documentation_file entries in test_reports? The schema says test_reports[]: id, date, pages, role. Documentation folder is not really a report with date/pages. Rule 8: don't fabricate. I could include them as test_reports with role "documentation_file" but date and pages unknown — omit those fields. Let me include them since role documentation_file exists.

Characteristics (Table 1, general):
- Flow rate range: See table 2
- Minimum measured quantity: 2 L
- Maximum pressure: 3.0 bar
- Environmental classes: M1 / E1
- Ambient temperature range: -25 °C / +55 °C; condensing humidity
- Product temperature range: -25 °C / +50 °C
- Intended for the measurement of: gasoline/gasoil or blend
- Power supply voltage: 230 / 400 V AC; 50 Hz
  → power_supply_voltage: {min: 230, max: 400}, V; power_supply_type: AC; power_supply_frequency: 50 Hz

Model family: The cert covers a family of configurations (Table 2). Configurations vary by number of gas separators/meters. These are configurations, not really models. The type is "Global Century" — one model. The table 2 is a configuration axis: number of gas separators and meters. So use config_level for flow rate ranges.

Configuration axis: configuration (1 x gas separator, 1 x meter etc.). Attribute: flow_rate_range. Values: {condition: "1 gas separator, 1 meter", value: {min: 4, max: 70}, unit_symbol: "L/min"} etc. Also could record intended product per configuration. Maybe better to preserve Table 2 in matrix_tables AND config_level.

Actually, rule 5 says: When attributes vary by configuration (not by model — e.g. 2-sensor-row vs 4-sensor-row setups; static vs dynamic weighing), use characteristics.config_level with axis describing the dimension.

So Table 2 → config_level entries with axis like "gas_separator_and_meter_configuration" and attribute "flow_rate_range". Also could add attribute "intended_measurement" per condition. Let me do:

config_level:
- attribute: "flow_rate_range", axis: "configuration", values: [
  {condition: "1 x gas separator, 1 x meter", value: {min:4, max:70}, unit_symbol:"L/min"},
  {condition: "1 x gas separator, 1 x meter (blending product)", value: {min:4, max:40}, unit_symbol:"L/min"},
  {condition: "1 x gas separator, 1 x meter (two measurement transducers)", value: {min:4, max:40}, unit_symbol:"L/min"},
  {condition: "1 x gas separator, 2 x meter", value: {min:4, max:90}, unit_symbol:"L/min"},

]

Also matrix_tables: preserve table 2 with columns configuration, flow_rate_range, remarks.

Components:
1. Measurement transducer, type iMeter, producer Wayne Fueling Systems Sweden AB. Characteristics: flow rate range 3–70 L/min, MMQ 2 L, max pressure 3.0 bar, environmental classes M1/E1, ambient temp -25/+55 °C, product temp -25/+50 °C, viscosity 0.4–8.0 mPa·s, pulser: WIP (WM001682-0001) or WIP (WM031856-0001) or XWIP (WM011529-0001) or XWIP II (WM019142-0001).
2. Measurement transducer, type Xflo™ (Xflo), same producer, flow 3–80 L/min, rest same.
3. Calculating/indicating device, type iGEM, producer Wayne Fueling Systems Sweden AB. Max volume indication 6 digits, max unit price 4 or 5 digits, max price to pay 6 or 7 digits, environmental M1/E1, ambient -40/+55 °C, software identification checksum 0BE5 or 555F, pulser same list.
4. Gas elimination device, type CPU, producer Wayne Fueling Systems Sweden AB. Max flow 90 L/min, min pressure 1.2 bar, max pressure 3.0 bar, environmental M1, ambient -25/+55, product -25/+50, viscosity 0.4–8.0 mPa·s.

The gas separator (combined pump and gas eliminator device) is also part of the dispenser. Also the calculator. The parts listed: measurement transducer (iMeter OR Xflo), calculating/indicating device (iGEM), gas elimination device (CPU). Alternatives: iMeter OR Xflo — the two measurement transducer types are alternatives. Hmm, they're separate components entries each. I can record alternatives "OR" for... Actually each components[] entry is separate; the alternatives field applies when cert offers alternatives within one entry. I could make one components entry for "Measurement transducer" with type_designations ["iMeter", "Xflo"] and alternatives "OR" — but the characteristics differ (flow range 3–70 vs 3–80). Better: two entries, each with its own characteristics. Alternatively one entry with sub-characteristics per type. I'll do two entries each with role "measurement_transducer" and their own characteristics.

Hmm, but schema: components[]: role, type_designations[], alternatives, characteristics{}. characteristics{} is free-form. Should the structured value form apply inside component characteristics? Probably yes for consistency. I'll use structured values there too.

Production locations: Wayne Fueling Systems Sweden AB (Malmö, Sweden), Wayne Indústria e Comércio (Rio de Janeiro, Brazil), Dresser Wayne Fuel Equipment (Shanghai) Co., Ltd (Shanghai, China). - environmental_class: "M1 / E1" (string) — could split into mechanical_environment_class M1 and climatic_environment_class E1. I'll use environment_class: "M1/E1"? That's interpreting M1/E1 per OIML D11 (M1 mechanical, E1 climatic). That's standard. But to be safe, keep environmental_class: "M1/E1" as string value. Hmm. The value would be string "M1 / E1". Fine.
- ambient_temperature_range: {min:-25, max:55} °C, note "condensing humidity" — footnote-ish. Could add footnote or separate characteristic ambient_conditions: "condensing humidity". I'll add footnote_markers? No footnote markers exist in doc. I could add a note field — schema doesn't have notes on values. Value must be object with value/unit_symbol/unit_id/footnote_markers. I could include extra key "note"? Schema says shape with those fields; adding "note" might violate strictness. I'll add a separate type_level characteristic: humidity: "condensing" — hmm. I'll add "humidity_conditions": {"value": "condensing humidity", "unit_symbol": null, "unit_id": null}. That preserves info.

Recommendation: id "R117-1", edition 2007? The recommendation is R 117-1 (2007). Edition: 2007. Hmm, edition (int). 2007. amendment: null. scheme: "A" or "B"? OIML certificates — the certificate number "R117/2007-NL1-16.04" — scheme A vs B refers to OIML CS (Certification System). Actually OIML-CS has two schemes: A and B. R117 certificates under scheme... Hmm. This is a standard OIML Certificate of Conformity (pre-CS or basic). The layered schema asks scheme (A|B). The older system (before 2018) had just OIML Certificates of Conformity; under OIML CS, certificates are issued under Scheme A (certificate of conformity) or Scheme B (type evaluation report...). Actually OIML-CS Scheme A = OIML Certificate of Conformity, Scheme B = OIML Type Evaluation Report. This document is a Certificate of Conformity. But is it under OIML-CS? Date 2016, before OIML-CS launched (2018). Hmm. The certificate format here is the traditional one. I'd say scheme "A" since it's a certificate of conformity. But not certain. Maybe safer to set scheme: "A" given it's a CoC. The instruction default? It says scheme (A|B). I'll put "A".
